description:
Landing a branch on a shared checkout forces the lead to commit other sessions' pending tracker lines, so tracker history misattributes work and commits carry state their author never reviewed.

## Background

Several sessions write `.jit/events.jsonl` in one primary checkout, and each leaves appended lines uncommitted until its own next tracker commit. A branch that changed the same log cannot merge there, because git refuses to overwrite a dirty file, even though the log uses the union merge driver. The only available route is to commit the log first, which publishes every other session's pending lines under the landing issue's attribution. Commit `99100d61e` did this deliberately to land 12a0a694. Commit `bbcf19b7d` did it by accident when filing that issue, since a tracker commit naming the log takes the whole file. Other sessions' issue records can be dirty in the same checkout, and an unrelated completion can sweep their readiness changes into the landing branch as well.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A landing never attributes another session's tracker lines to its own issue: pending tracker state lands in its own neutral commit before the merge.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every tracker commit a landing makes publishes a coherent `.jit` state, taken under the repository write lock, and a leftover redo record refuses the landing.
- [hard] REQ-03: One command, `jit worktree land <branch>`, performs the landing through `storage::git` (`@/charter/D-21`). It supports `--json`, refuses clearly without git, bounds its lock wait with a loud timeout, makes no sync commit when nothing is pending, and on a merge conflict aborts the merge, keeps the sync commit, names the conflicted paths and exits nonzero with no retry.
- [hard] REQ-04: The landing prose and steps the command replaces are removed from the skills, and `git add .jit` is swept where the command supersedes it. Net lines are reported.

## Notes

Mechanism ruled by the invoker after a tested round. Per-writer logs and a gitignored log were rejected: the first rewords two invariants and adds about 250 lines, and the second contradicts `@/charter/D-1`. Publishing only one's own event lines was rejected because a commit holding one writer's lines cannot be coherent with `index.json` and issue records (`@/inv/derived-state-coherence`).

Each session working in its own linked checkout (option 4) was tested on a scratch clone and failed: concurrent creates conflict on `index.json`, same-issue edits and the same promoted dependent conflict on the issue record, in 4 of 4 runs per scenario. Leases stayed exclusive across checkouts. A stale view in that layout let a second session take a closed issue's lease; this applies only to that rejected layout and needs no action.

A conflict on `index.json` is a loud refusal until the separate index-membership task lands; `aeafc378` does not wait on it.
title: Land branches without committing other sessions' pending tracker lines
